title: Initializer Validation Profile
purpose: Defines the stable ordered set of Version 1 validation checks, each with a stable ID, classification, order, pass condition, and failure-code vocabulary. Together these checks determine whether the staged repository is eligible for promotion.

checks.pass_condition: The canonical bootstrap request is schema_version 2 and contains exactly schema_version and destination.
The destination is canonical absolute local-path input and the carried canonical bytes/fingerprint are unchanged.
The bootstrap request contains no legacy authority, source, product, profile, or direction-material fields.
The source.repository path resolves to an existing local directory that is a valid Git repository (contains a .git/ directory or equivalent).
The source repository's native object format (reported by git rev-parse --show-object-format) is sha1.
The source revision resolves to a valid commit object in the local source repository via `git rev-parse --verify <revision>^{commit}`.

The exact source commit exists locally. Every source_path declared in the material manifest is reachable from the commit tree root and resolves to exactly one Git blob or supported symlink. Every blob or symlink referenced by a declared source_path exists as a local object. No material-manifest entry declares source_type tree. Undeclared source-directory descendants have no effect on initialized output because the output inventory, not the source tree, determines every output path.

The material manifest at product/scripts/initializer/framework-inventory.json in the source commit tree validates against the material-manifest contract schema (product.material-manifest), including material_key uniqueness.
Every source_path declared in the material manifest exists at the expected source_type (blob or symlink) in the source commit tree, and no entry declares source_type tree.

Every material_key in the material manifest has a matching material_index entry in the output inventory, and every material_index entry in the output inventory has a matching material_key in the material manifest. No orphan keys and no unused entries. No material_index entry has a destination_path that resolves to a Git tree object (mode 040000).
Every entry in the output inventory (fixed worktree file with required true, material_index entry, resolved dynamic family path) is present in the staged repository.

Every observed worktree path in the staged repository matches exactly one output-inventory entry (fixed file, material_index entry, or resolved dynamic family path) and no prohibited path exists under its matching rule. No installed path claims membership as a descendant of a directory-valued material_index entry because tree-valued entries are not permitted.
Product Level workspace README files are not required during repository bootstrap.

Every file produced by copy-verbatim (material_index entries with operation copy-verbatim) has byte content identical to its corresponding source Git blob, resolved by matching material_key between the output inventory and the material manifest at the declared source revision.
No product direction evidence is required during repository bootstrap.
The bootstrap-generated provenance and handoff records are present and valid JSON objects.
No product template documents are generated during repository bootstrap.
The SHA-256 content digest of the repository/ subtree (excluding .git/) matches the expected digest recorded in the staging-state record.
The provenance record uses schema version 2 and matches the resolved framework repository/revision and bootstrap request fingerprint.
The handoff manifest at repo/initializer/handoff.json correctly describes the repository state: its arrays are disjoint, cover every non-foundation file, and have lexicographic ordering.
The repository's active branch name matches the bootstrap profile constant (main for standard-v1).
The repository contains exactly one root commit with no parent.
The root commit author name and email match the bootstrap profile constants (author_name and author_email for standard-v1).
The root commit message matches the bootstrap profile commit_message constant.
The Git worktree inside the repository/ directory has no unstaged changes and no untracked files.
The repository has zero configured Git remotes.

normative_requirements.text: The validation profile shall declare a stable ordered set of checks, each with a unique check_id, classification (required or advisory), deterministic order number, applies_to scope, pass_condition, and an explicit list of failure_codes.
A required check that produces a status of failed or error shall cause overall validation to fail and shall block promotion.
An advisory check that produces a status of failed or error shall be recorded in the validation report but shall not cause overall validation to fail or block promotion.

The validation profile shall be versioned via profile_version. Successor versions may add new checks at new order numbers without renumbering existing checks. No check_id shall be removed from a published profile version; a check may be deprecated but shall remain defined.

Every check in the profile must apply to one of the following scopes: request, source, material-manifest, repository-worktree, or git-state. Checks are executed in two phases: Phase 1 (input and source, orders 10-70) and Phase 2 (staged repository and Git state, orders 80-200). Each phase executes checks in ascending order number within that phase. No ordinary check may read or validate content under transaction/; staging-state validation is not an ordinary profile check.

After all Phase 1 and Phase 2 checks are complete, report finalization is a deterministic ordered write operation that shall proceed in this exact order: (a) calculate the proposed overall_status (pass when every required Phase 1 and Phase 2 check has status passed, otherwise fail); (b) construct in memory a proposed final validation report carrying the proposed overall_status, the request fingerprint computed once by request intake under product.initialization-request::INIT-REQ-012 and carried unchanged by the validated request model, and the expected repository_content_digest from the output.repository-digest-match check; (c) construct in memory a proposed final staging-state representation carrying validation_completed equal to true, validation_overall_status equal to the proposed overall_status, the same unchanged request fingerprint, and the expected repository_content_digest; (d) validate the proposed staging-state representation against the product.staging-state schema in memory without writing it; (e) validate the proposed validation report against the validation-report schema in memory, verifying the request_fingerprint linkage, the repository_content_digest linkage, and check ordering and uniqueness; (f) serialize and write the finalized validation report atomically to transaction/validation-report.json; (g) serialize and write the finalized staging-state record atomically to transaction/staging-state.json; and (h) re-read or otherwise verify that the two durable records are mutually consistent, confirming they share the same request_fingerprint and repository_content_digest and that the staging-state validation_completed and validation_overall_status agree with the completed validation result. Report finalization shall not reserialize the request or recompute its fingerprint. These postconditions are not ordinary profile checks; they are validation-component invariants enforced during report finalization before promotion. Any failure in steps (a) through (h) shall prevent promotion.

Promotion is permitted only when both the finalized validation report and the finalized staging-state record are durably written and verified mutually consistent, the report validates against its schema, every required Phase 1 and Phase 2 check has status passed, and overall_status is pass. Promotion must not begin when only one of the two records has been durably written. Report finalization failure (staging-state schema validation failure, fingerprint mismatch, digest mismatch, validation-status mismatch, report schema validation failure, serialization failure, linkage mismatch, or failure of the final consistency verification) shall prevent promotion and shall be recorded as a pre-promotion failure with the staging transaction root preserved for diagnostics.
